answers.question: Why inVision U?
answers.answer: I want to build products that people in my city actually use. At school I led our robotics team to the regional final, and I always ask everyone's opinion before I decide anything. inVision U is where I can learn to do this at a bigger scale.

answers.question: Describe a time you led others.
answers.answer: I organised a weekend clean-up with twelve volunteers and split them into three teams. Each team had a leader and a list of streets. We finished by two and collected forty bags.

answers.question: Tell us about something that did not go as planned.
answers.answer: Our robot broke two days before the final. We rebuilt the arm overnight and still made it. I learned to always have spare parts.

answers.question: What problem in your community would you like to solve?
answers.answer: Public transport in Almaty is hard to plan. I want to make an app that shows real bus times.

answers.question: How would you rate your English?
answers.answer: C2. I speak fluently and read everything in English.

answers.response: I prefer to decide quickly and explain my reasons later.
When a teammate disagrees, I focus on finishing the task first.

simulationTurns.speaker: character
simulationTurns.text: Honestly, I'm done. Timur rewrote my whole module last night without a word to me. If my work can just be thrown away, why am I even here? Maybe the three of you can finish the demo without me.

simulationTurns.speaker: candidate
simulationTurns.text: Okay, let's fix this fast. The demo is in three days, so we can't lose you now. Send me the list of what Timur changed and I'll look at it tonight.

simulationTurns.speaker: character
simulationTurns.text: Okay… I hear you. But it isn't only about the code. Nobody asked me anything. How do I know it won't happen again next week?

simulationTurns.speaker: candidate
simulationTurns.text: From now on nobody merges into someone else's module without a review from its owner. I'll set that rule in the repo today.

simulationTurns.speaker: character
simulationTurns.text: Fine, I could talk to him. But the demo is in three days and his version still breaks the login. Who decides which version we keep?

simulationTurns.speaker: candidate
simulationTurns.text: We keep your version for the demo because it works. Timur moves his changes to a separate branch and we look at them after Thursday. If his login fix is really needed, the risk is that we demo with a known bug, so I'll ask him to patch only that.

simulationTurns.speaker: character
simulationTurns.text: That sounds fair, I guess. So what do I actually do today? I don't want to sit around waiting for Timur to agree with me.

simulationTurns.speaker: candidate
simulationTurns.text: Today you finish the payment endpoint, Timur fixes the login in his branch, and I write the demo script. We freeze the backend by Thursday noon and do a full run at six.

simulationTurns.speaker: character
simulationTurns.text: Alright. If we write down who owns what, I'm in. But you tell Timur, not me. I don't want another argument tonight.

simulationTurns.speaker: candidate
simulationTurns.text: Deal. I'll put the owners in the team chat in ten minutes and call Timur right after. If the Thursday run fails, we cut the analytics screen instead of working all night.

simulationTurns.speaker: character
simulationTurns.text: Okay. Let's try it your way. And thanks for actually listening.
